quest.name: No Name on the Work Roll

stages.journal: I woke in the hold of a ship at a pier west of Lilmoth, in Black Marsh, among a gang of Argonians I do not know. I'm to go up the stairs and out onto the pier, where the man who keeps the gang's work roll stands.
Buys-The-Months, the broker on the pier, is dead before he said a word to me, and nobody else on the pier will send a stranger anywhere. I'm to look for work in Lilmoth, east along the shore.

Buys-The-Months, the broker who holds the gang's Owing, the months of work they owe, has no line for me on his roll. I owe him nothing, so he will not keep me. He says a woman called Nesh-Deeka, a guest at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth, pays for work from anyone off his ship. I'm to find her there.

Nesh-Deeka serves the Veiled Reed, the ruling state's quiet service. The gang carried me off the bank the night their camp burned, she says, when a woman with a knotted cord killed her courier, took his satchel and let me live. She wants a hand nobody can claim. I'm to tell her whether I will work for the Reed.
I took work with the Veiled Reed. Nesh-Deeka put fifty gold in my hand and told me what the Reed wants first. Why the woman with the knotted cord let me live, nobody has told me yet.
Nesh-Deeka, the Veiled Reed's handler in Lilmoth, is dead. Whatever the Reed wanted of me died with her.

quest.name: The Tree That Turned Its Face

stages.journal: Nesh-Deeka has word that the Hist of Low-Reed Village, a stilt village east of Lilmoth along the shore, has turned its face. She wants to know whether the cell that cut the cutting's roots at the burnt camp did this too. I'm to go to Low-Reed Village and speak to Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald, who speaks for the village to strangers.

Hires-By-The-Season says Low-Reed Village's Hist shut eleven nights ago and the eggs in its pool died. The village blames the leeches at its roots, and Pays-Late, the tree-minder, who stands by the roots under the stilts day and night and will not say why. I'm to get the truth out of Pays-Late.
Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald of Low-Reed Village, is dead. Pays-Late, the tree-minder, keeps the Hist from the bank under the stilts. I'm to ask him what happened to it.

Pays-Late told me the truth. The Hist's root was cut, its sap drawn off and the cut sealed with his own gum. He hid it, fearing the village would call it his work. A boat came from the north reeds that night. I'm to cross the leech water north and take back the sap.

I leaned on Pays-Late with the village's blame until he told me; he will not forget it. The Hist's root was cut, its sap drawn off and the cut sealed with his own gum. He hid it, fearing the blame. A boat came from the north reeds. I'm to cross the leech water north and take back the sap.

I took the jars of the Hist's sap from two men on the dry rise, jars like the one the cutters dropped at the burnt camp: the cell did this. The jars are Pays-Late's to pour back, or proof of the cell's work for Nesh-Deeka. I'm to bring them to Pays-Late and decide.
I told Pays-Late the jars go to the people I work for, as proof of the cell's work, and kept them. His tree stays dark. I'm to bring them to Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth.

I gave the jars to Pays-Late and kept his secret. He will pour the sap back at the cut root, and the village will go on blaming the leeches. The cell drew this tree's sap into jars, as it drew the cutting's. What does it want with it?

I gave the jars to Pays-Late on one condition, that he tells Hires-By-The-Season himself that he found the cut and hid it, and he gave his word. He will pour the sap back at the cut root. The cell drew this tree's sap into jars, as it drew the cutting's. What does it want with it?

I gave the jars to Nesh-Deeka, and she paid me fifty gold. She keeps them as proof of the cell's work. Low-Reed Village's Hist stays dark, and the village still blames Pays-Late. The cell drew that tree's sap into jars, as it drew the cutting's. What does it want with it?
Pays-Late, the tree-minder of Low-Reed Village, is dead. Whatever happened to his tree, nobody there will tell a stranger now.

stages.journal: I have seen a Hist cut at the root, and its sap in the cell's jars. I'm to tell Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth what I found at Low-Reed Village.

Nesh-Deeka says the tree-minders and Nisswo of the interior meet at Helstrom, behind the marsh, and carry news home. She wants them to hear what a cut Hist looks like from someone the Reed can deny, so I go alone and do not name the Reed. I'm to take the coast ship from Lilmoth's stop to Helstrom's landing.

I came ashore at Helstrom's river landing. The way in is root and shallows, where Nesh-Deeka says giant wasps nest. In the grove past the city's gate stand Ei-Tuja, a Nisswo who reads for anyone, and Kaska-Meen, a tree-minder who hears few strangers. I'm to tell Ei-Tuja what I saw, or ask him to bring Kaska-Meen to hear it.
Ei-Tuja says the tree-minders will hear a cut tree's story only from someone worth hearing, and has left it to me. I'm to tell Kaska-Meen myself, if I can talk her round.
Kaska-Meen will not hear it from me. Ei-Tuja, the Nisswo, still will. I'm to tell him what I saw.

I told Kaska-Meen what I saw at Low-Reed Village, and the tree-minders will hear it from her and guard their trees. She told me what a dying Hist leaves: a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap holding its memories, once used to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Is that what the cell is gathering sap for?

I told Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village, and he will preach it openly in every village he walks to. He told me what a dying Hist leaves: a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap holding its memories, once used to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Is that what the cell is gathering sap for?
Ei-Tuja, the Nisswo who would carry any word to the villages, is dead. With him went the one voice in Helstrom sure to say what I saw at Low-Reed Village.
Nesh-Deeka, the Veiled Reed's handler in Lilmoth, is dead. Whatever the Reed wanted said in Helstrom died with her.

lines: Slaughterfish swim in the water just north of my lily pads, and more just south-west. They take the catch off my line. Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore just south-south-west, so keep out of the water, dry-foot.
Lilmoth? Follow the shore east a fair way and Lilmoth is there. Keep to the bank and out of the water, dry-foot.
Hereguard Plantation? Follow the path west just until you reach the dead tree. Then follow the path south-west a short way, and Hereguard is there. I buy my bait there.
Ah, you came back, my friend. Sit on the bank and watch the pads with me.
Dry-foot. Keep to the bank and do not splash. The fish are feeding.
Wild leeks grow on the bank a short way east-south-east of here. Take them from the bank and not from my lily pads, dry-foot.
A giant crab lives in the shallows a short way south-south-west, and he is called Old Salty. I will say no more about him to a dry-foot I do not know.
I am Uleesh. I fish the shallows below the walls and sell my catch inside. The rent inside is more than I can get for fish, so I stay out here. Twenty years on the same water now.
Thorn? Walk south-west a short way and you will reach it, outlander. It is no great trouble if you are not stopped.
Ah, my friend. Come, stand here by me; nobody is counting us just now. What do you need?
Outlander. If you are counting something, count it elsewhere. What do you want?
The house is just north-west of here, outlander. I labour there. So do the rest of us who owe.
The Dres raided Thorn for slaves, long ago. That raid made them the first of the great Dunmer families in the trade. Curse them softly, outlander. Softly.
Folk of Thornmarsh learn a little magic, just enough to get by. Nothing a guard need hear of. I will say no more on it.
Doveth Aralen. I was born owing, outlander. My mother's account came to me with her name. I have worked off three seasons and been charged for four.
Jeelus-Vax is the guard captain over the east houses. You will find him just south-south-west of here. Fair enough, for a guard.
The big ship? Walk south a short way and you will have it in front of you, outlander. You cannot miss a ship.
Ah, the one face in Thorn that has never asked me for coin. Sit if you like; the people here will not charge you for the ground. Yet.
Well, outlander. Come to look at the labour, or to buy some?
Yes, outlander? If it is coin you are after, you have found the wrong man.
This place? A few houses and a great many debts. There is a house just north-north-west of here, if it is a roof you want. Whose roof it is, I could not say.

Black Marsh, outlander? Dunmer and Argonian labourers are held under the same ledger here, and the old Archein managers who kept the accounts assess every Owing. Even-handed, you might say, so long as you are not the one owing.
Thorn has a good many Dunmer in it, you will notice. And how many families do you think have not got a grandparent on each side of the coffles? Ask the next man you pass, and watch his face.

Myself? I came to Thorn a free man, outlander, to trade. Then I lost a wager I could not pay, and my Owing has been sold once already. As for the rest, my grandmother was Argonian on one side, and I could not tell you which side I am on.
Mils Ganthis? Another Dunmer under an Owing. Look just south-south-west of here and listen; you will hear him before you see him. That man never could keep his mouth shut.
My trade? I am held under an Owing, outlander. A man can be sold along with it and never told who holds it. So when you ask what I do, you might ask who I do it for.
Oh, it is you. Come, sit a moment, my friend. I have been wanting someone to talk to, and I promise I won't say anything foolish this time. Well, not much.
Oh. Hello. I don't think we have met, have we? I am Mils Ganthis. Forgive me, I talk too much when I am nervous, and I am nearly always nervous.

Thorn is not much to look at, and I am sorry for it, though it is hardly my doing. The signpost is just west-south-west of where I am standing, if you want to know which way is which. I would not like you to lose your way.

Black Marsh? I am no scholar, outlander. Only a cook, or I was. I can tell you how an Owing goes, though. It grows. Spoilage, breakage, sickness, even what the debtor eats to stay alive: all of it is added to the account. Please don't tell anyone I said so.
Me? There is little enough to tell. I was a cook in Tear, a good one, I think, until the Owing found me. Now I cook nothing and eat what is charged to me. I am sorry, that is more than you asked.

Nalvos Brenur is just north-north-east of where I stand. He is a labourer under an Owing, the same as me. He hates me and he is right to, though I would rather not say why. If you want sense, ask Doveth Aralen, the wisest man in Thorn. Severan Otho is kind, I will say that for him.

I was a cook, and I miss it more than I can say, the smells most of all. Now I am a labourer, and every meal a labourer eats goes on his account. Every one. A decent bowl that costs me nothing, that is all I want. Forgive me, I am rambling.
I give no advice to strangers, outlander; I will say only this. Past the hut, a short way south-south-east of here, the guards do not watch the ground. Take that as you like.
Temple Pass, outlander? The dead tree stands just north of here; make for it. Beyond it, keep north over open ground a long walk, and Temple Pass is there.
You want Temple Pass. Walk north to the dead tree, which you can see from here, and go on north from it across the open ground. It is a long walk, and the pass is at the end of it.
Rest a moment. I am glad of the sight of you. I will see to the work later.
Stand with me a while, if you have the time. There is no one to hurry you here.
Outlander. State your business, and I will tell you whether I can help.
Good day, outlander. I have work waiting, so be brief.
We work here under an Owing, outlander. To most of us that is all this place is. I stand between the house and the cooking fire. The fire is just south-east of here.
Ask Nalvos Brenur how the ledger of Thorn is kept, outlander. I know only that my father's Owing is written in it, and that the Tax Heel carry it.
There is a painting in Thorn called the Slave-Coffles. It shows the city's worst day, and no one who sees it forgets it. I have seen it, and it is the same thing with better manners.
Tolyn Vedram, outlander. I carry my father's Owing, and I mean to be the last of my family to owe. When Doveth Aralen is tired, I keep the other labourers calm.
Doveth Aralen is the eldest of the labourers in the house. You will find him just north-north-west of here. He is a Dunmer, held under an Owing as I am. I respect him, so speak with care.
Cage Door? Take the path west a short way, and it is just past the dead tree. Keep your hands where I can see them on the way, outlander.
You again. Good. The watch has been quiet, and I will not complain of that. Sit a while, my friend, if you have the time.
Outlander. State your business. I keep the guard at the east houses, and I want no trouble here.
These are the east houses, where the Dunmer labourers sleep. I keep the guard over them. The hut stands a short way south-south-east of the houses, if you need a roof.
When the Dres left, their holdings passed to whoever was standing in them. Who holds the title is still argued. I do not take a side. I take my pay and keep the watch.
I am Jeelus-Vax, captain of the guard here. I would rather be fair than kind. Now, what do you want?
Quill-Teeth, the Tax Heel collector of Owings, is just north of here. Quill-Teeth pushes too hard, in my view. Go carefully.
One face I know in a crowd of faces I do not. Stand by the doors with me a while.
One visitor. I do not know you. Say what you want, and say it plainly.
This is the west side of town, visitor. I watch the cages and count who is in them at every change of guard. The cage door stands just west-north-west of here, where I do my counting.
Magic? Ask Doveth Aralen about what folk learn of it in Thornmarsh, visitor. I learned a little as a hatchling, to keep warm. That is all I will say of it.

I do not share this with strangers, visitor. I count my words as I count everything else. One cage holds someone who is in no count. Its door is just west-north-west of here, and that is all I will say.
I am Counts-The-Bars. I guard the cage doors on the west side. I trust numbers more than people, and I do not apologise for it.
Rufio Casca, soldier of the hired Imperial company, stands just west-north-west of here, close by the cage door. He stands too near the cages.
The big ship, traveller? Keep to the boards and go south a short way, and you will see the ship there.
Traveller, a face I know, at my signposts! Stand with me a while, and I will tell you the whole of Avumar again, from the beginning.
Traveller. Stop a moment. I stand at these signposts, and I can tell you where each of them leads.
The dock lies just south-south-east of these signposts, traveller. I keep my eye on it, because that is where smoke would come from.

Thorn was razed once, traveller. A Naga named Avumar struck a bargain with a Dremora, and the city burned for it. I say the Tax Heel, the collectors the field-owners send for what they are owed and for tolls, will bring us another burning, and I do not say it lightly.
I am Ukka-Meesh, traveller. I stand at the signposts in the middle of Thorn and tell people where things are, and I know the story of Avumar for anyone who will stand still and hear it.
Xeech-Nu is just west of these signposts, traveller. He guards the centre of the town with me. He is a good listener, and hears a story to its end.
Thorn? It lies just north-north-west of this dock, in plain sight, traveller.
Good, you are one I need not question. Come and stand by me while I count. What have you brought this time?
Traveller. What do you carry?
Stand clear of the crates, traveller. State your business and what is in your pack.

This is the south dock, and the big ship lies just south of it, beside my post. Nothing comes off that ship that I do not count. The company of Aulus Varrenius does not let me aboard. I think Aulus Varrenius hides something there.
The villages around Thorn belonged to the Archeins. They kept their accounts better than they kept faith. My family worked for them, and we still keep their habits.
I am Holds-The-Tally. I keep the south dock and count every crate that comes off the ships. I am paid by the cargo, so I count it twice.
Gaius Fennic, a soldier of the Imperial company, stands just north of this dock. He is honest, and I would trust his count.

Temple Pass? Go north a short way, and you will see a dead tree on your left. Keep north a fair way, and the stone tower stands on your left. Then climb north-west over open ground, a fair way. Temple Pass is there.
It is good to see you again, my friend. Stand with me a while. I am watching the road.
Stranger. Say what you need.
What is it, stranger? I am watching the road.
I keep this corner and watch the road north. Look just south-west of my post. That is the hut.
The Tear road leaves Thorn to the north, for Morrowind. Traders use it to earn coin, and that is all there is to it. I came from a village on that road.
I am Sheel-Taza. I guard the south-west corner. I came from a village up the Tear road, and I find Thorn too loud.
Look just north-east of my corner. Lucan Sevro, the archer of the hired Imperial company, is there. He is reckless with his bow, stranger. He shoots too near the huts.
Listen well, hatchling. Follow the path north a fair way, and you will come to the stone tower.
Hm. You stopped for an old guard. Stand with me a while. The watch is long, and I would sooner spend it with someone who remembers me.
What do you want, hatchling? Say it plainly. I am on watch.
Hm. A new face. Speak, and do not keep me long.
This is Thorn, hatchling. I have stood guard in it longer than anyone. If you are lost, the signpost is just north of where I stand.
Ask Doveth Aralen, a good Dunmer, about what the Dres did here, hatchling. I remember it myself, and I say so to anyone who will hear. I have not forgiven them, though they are long gone.
I am Old Mossback, hatchling. I have watched over Thorn longer than any other guard. The green on my scales gave me the name. In all those years no one has once thanked me for it.
Bites-The-Coin stands guard at the centre of town, just east-south-east of me. That one is a disgrace to the watch.
Some advice, traveller: anyone who goes down the dock just south of here goes unseen by me, for a price. I take coin, and that is no secret.
It is the bridge you want, traveller. Follow the path north-west a short way until you reach the signpost on your left. Then walk west a short way, and the bridge is there.
You want the bridge, traveller. Take the path north-west a short way, until the signpost stands on your left. From the signpost go west a short way, and you will see the bridge.
Ah, traveller, one purse I will not test! Come, stand with me a while. It is good to see a face I know.
Traveller. Mind your purse in Thorn, and say what you want.
Good day, traveller. Those are fine boots. What is your business?
This is the middle of Thorn, and I stand where the signposts are. The signpost is just south of here, traveller; you will not miss it.
Thorn is called the Jewel of the East, traveller, as deadly as it is beautiful. Purses go missing here, and the guards look away. I am one of them, and I do not pretend otherwise.
They call me Bites-The-Coin, traveller, because I test every coin with my teeth. I take coin to look away, as the guards of Thorn always have, and I do not hide it.
If you are looking for a sellsword, traveller, try Tertius Vallo. He serves with the Imperial sellswords, and he stands just south-south-west of here.
Traveller, the cooking fire just north-east of here is banked each night. Keep sparks away from the huts.
Mind the huts on this side, traveller. The cooking fire just north-east of here is banked each night; carry no sparks from it to the huts.
The stone tower, traveller? Climb north-west from the huts a short way, and you will come to it. Go softly.
Climb north-west from here a short way; you will see the stone tower. Keep your voice low.
It is you; keep your voice low. Sit by me a while; all is quiet tonight, and it is good to have company.
Softly, traveller. Sparks carry, and so do voices. What do you want?
Traveller. I have not slept, and I will not tonight. Say what you need, and say it low.
These are the huts of the north-east side, traveller. The cooking fire is just north-east of here, by the huts; keep well clear of it.
Ask Ukka-Meesh about Avumar, traveller. He tells the story right. I believe it. I fear the burning will come again.
I do not tell the tale of Avumar myself, traveller. Ukka-Meesh tells it better, and it is not a tale for loud voices. Sparks carry.
Tsatheel. I keep the huts on this side, and the fire. I rarely sleep, traveller; someone must watch.
Quill-Teeth is a Tax Heel, traveller: the one who collects the Owings. You will find Quill-Teeth just south-south-west of here.
I hoped you would pass this way. Stand a while by the door with me. It is quiet, and I am glad of company.
Stranger. I guard these cages. Say what you want, and say it softly.
I guard the cages on the west side, stranger. It is not work I would choose. The signpost is just west-south-west of the post where I stand at the cage doors.
I came down the Tear road years ago, stranger. Ask Sheel-Taza about the road and its trade. I know it only as the way I came, and I would sooner speak of something else.
There is something I do not tell strangers, and I will not tell it to you yet. Come back when I know you better.
At night I carry water to the cage door just west-south-west of the post where I stand. I would not have it spoken of.
I am Wazei-Ru. I stand at these doors with Counts-The-Bars. I would rather be posted anywhere else.
Ilvesa Drethan is a Dunmer held in a long Owing, a debt worked off in service. People call her a slave. From the cages where I stand she is just north-north-west, and I think well of her.
The bridge, visitor? Walk north-west from here for a fair way. The walk is easy enough, so take it slowly.
Looking for the bridge? Go north-west for a fair way, and there it is.
Come and sit with me out of the sun, if you have a mind to. I have all the keys on my belt today, and that is a good day.
Visitor. I keep the keys to the west cages here, so do not ask me for anything that needs a hurry.
Visitor, these are the west cages, and the huts beside them. The cage door stands just north-east of here, there in sight.
It is a quiet post, and I like it quiet, visitor. If you want the cage door, it is just north-east of here, in sight.
An Owing is a debt a man works off in labour, visitor. It can be sold: the one who is owed sells it on, and the debtor's work goes with it. Such sales are common enough.
I am Keeps-The-Lock, visitor. I hold the keys to the west cages, and I lose them more often than I should. I am not a cruel man, only a slow one.
Counts-The-Bars watches the cage doors on the west side. Go a short way east-north-east of here, and you will find him. Visitor, he is a nag: he reports every key I lose.
A known face. That is rare enough to welcome. Stand easy; the houses are quiet and I have time to talk.
Outlander. I guard these houses. State your business and keep to the path.
These houses are mine to watch, and the cages behind them. The house stands just north-north-east of here, in plain sight.
The Barsaebic Ayleids founded Thorn, before any Dunmer or Argonian held it. Since then it has had too many masters, outlander. I would see it ruled by people born in it.
I do not tell this to strangers. Among the cages behind the houses, the far door lies just south-south-east of here. It is the one that is not checked at night.
I am Ma-Veesk. I guard the north-west houses and the cages behind them. At home I speak Jel, and I have little else to say of myself.
Two-Bells shares the watch here. Look for Two-Bells just south-south-west of here, close beside the houses I guard.
The stone tower, traveller? Ha! Climb north a short way, and the tower is there.
Ho, there is my favourite traveller! Come, stand by me and tell me everything. What news do you bring from the road?
Ho, traveller! You heard my bells coming, did you not? Everyone does. What news do you bring?
A stranger! Speak up, traveller, I like a loud voice. I do not know your accent, so where have you come from?
This place, traveller? These are the north-west houses, and I guard them. The house stands just east of here.
Black Marsh, traveller? I walked the Tear road for years, guarding carts. For the trade on it, ask Sheel-Taza; I only walked beside the carts. Now, what news do you bring?

I am Two-Bells! The two bells on my belt gave me the name, so that I never sneak up on anyone. For years I guarded carts on the Tear road, and I like travellers still. The Imperials are the best company, I find.
Ma-Veesk? Ma-Veesk stands guard at the north-west houses too, just north-north-east of here. Far too serious for my taste, traveller.
Stand here, if you wish. I say that to very few, so do not make me regret it.
Outlander. Say what you want and be brief; I am a slave, not a guide.
What do you want, outlander? Speak plainly. I have no use for pleasantries.
This is Thorn, outlander. I am held in it. There is a house just east of where I stand; look at it if you must, I will not walk you there.
Black Marsh? Ask Doveth Aralen about the Dres, outlander. I know their history and my own part in it, and you will get it more gently from Doveth than from me.
Ask Keeps-The-Lock how an Owing is sold, outlander. Mine has been sold twice, and Keeps-The-Lock bought part of one. I think of Keeps-The-Lock as a merchant in flesh.
I tell this to no stranger, outlander. I will not tell it twice. My brother was sold away on the big ship, a short way south of here.
Myself? Ilvesa Drethan, a slave, outlander; the word is honest and I prefer honest words. My Owing has been sold twice, and each time it carried me further from my family.
Wazei-Ru stands at the cage doors on the west side, just south-south-east of where I stand. Kind, for a guard. Do not mistake that for much.
The big ship lies a short way south, outlander. Keep walking and you will reach it.
South, outlander, a short way. The big ship is there.
Ah, you. Sit a moment. Have you eaten? You look thinner.
Outlander. Ask what you need to ask, and I will answer if I can.
Hm. Outlander. Speak plainly. I am tired.
You will find the signpost just south-south-east of here, outlander.
Heita-Meen was a slave of Thorn, outlander. Heita-Meen killed Councillor Glathis Dres and took the Archein guard by duel. The freeing of the Argonians began here.
What is charged on an Owing is for Mils Ganthis to tell, outlander. I am tired, and I will not say it badly.
I am Fendyl Omoren. I carry an Owing, outlander. It has grown so long that its charges outnumber my work.
Most call me a slave, outlander. I have heard the name of Heita-Meen. I no longer think about walking away.
Ukka-Meesh is the guard at the town's centre, outlander, just south-south-east of here.
In a labourer's account the days of food outnumber the days of work, outlander. They always do.
I labour under my Owing. In my account the days I eat always outnumber the days I work.
Lilmoth Dock, walker. Go north-east a fair way. The burnt-out house stands on the way, and the dock lies past it.
Lilmoth lies north, walker. It is a fair way on foot. We stay clear of its rents.
Walker, my friend, welcome. Sit by the spit. There is always a place here for you.
Walker. You stand at our spit. Say what you want and I will hear it.

This is our village, walker. A few families live on the marsh outside Lilmoth. The cooking spit stands in the middle of the village. From the spit, the carpenter's bench is just south-south-east and a food barrel just east-south-east.
We keep a second hearth just west of this spit, on the west edge of the village. It has food barrels, a cooking pot and a bed. They belong to the families.
Lilmoth has no single ruler. A council of powerful merchants governs it and pays guards to patrol the streets. I want no seat among them. So it is.
In Lilmoth people take their quarrels to their elders, retired Shadowscales among them, not to a court. We do the same here. The elders speak at this spit.
I am Flaa Heet. I lead the families who live here. I stand at the spit because every quarrel and every catch comes to it in the end.
Tseeta has her stall just north of this spit. She haggles too hard, and the village is better for her anyway. Okeeh-Jas sells from hers, just south-south-west.
It is you, it is you! Did you see the boats come in? Huge, the big one, huge!
Who are you, big one? Where did you come from? What are you carrying? Is any of it shiny?

Leeks? Wild leeks grow just north-west of here, close by the fish barrels. I hate the fish barrels because they smell. Emperor Parasol Moss hangs a short way north, big one. I have not been told what it is for.
This is our village, big one. Look, a rowboat, drawn up just east-north-east of here. It is a huge boat. I am not going to ask you for a ride.
I am Peeks-Under-Boats. I look at everything, and I run errands. One day I will be a boat captain, big one. I practise on the frogs. They do not obey me yet.

Flaa Heet, the headman, is usually by the cooking spit, just south of here. He knows a great deal, big one. Hums-To-The-Rain is just south-south-west, on the west side of the village. Hums-To-The-Rain sings too much.

Soulrest, buyer? That is where the real coin is. Follow the shore north-east, a short way past the rowing boat, until the burnt-out house is on your right. Walk north-east a short way to the big ship, then follow the shore north-east a short way until Lilmoth Dock is on your right. From there climb south-east a fair way. Soulrest is there. Good trade.

Hereguard? Walk north-west a fair way until Lilmoth is on your right. Then follow the shore west a short way until you reach the dead tree on your right. Walk south-west a short way from the tree, and Hereguard Plantation is there.
Good trade comes back. Come closer and I will set aside the best of the day for you before anyone else sees it. Okeeh-Jas does not need to hear about it.
Buyer. You came in from the dock, so mine is the first stall you have met. Look here before you look anywhere else.
I am Tseeta. I sell the village's surplus to whoever walks in from the dock. I took the north side so that I meet buyers before Okeeh-Jas does.
Food and small goods, buyer. Show me your coin and I will name a price. Good trade.
Okeeh-Jas has the other stall, just south of mine. You can see it from here. Watch how she smiles when she names her price, buyer.
I sell what the village has left over, buyer: fish, roots and small goods. The fish is in the barrels just north-north-west of my stall, in sight, if you want to look before you buy.
Mm, I know your step. Sit by the nets with me, friend. The rope is dry enough for talking.
Mm. Traveller. Mind the nets. They are still wet.
Gourds grow a short way north-north-east of here, and so does a swamp fungal pod. Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow in one patch the same short way off. Mm, take only what is ripe, traveller.
I mend the nets on the west side, where they dry. The villagers keep a meat barrel out on the marsh, a short way north-north-west of here. Hm, I would sooner walk that way than inside Lilmoth.
Mm. An Argonian kept long from their own Hist fades. The colour thins and the markings go soft. They come back when the person goes home.
I am Hums-To-The-Rain. I mend the nets and gather what grows on the marsh. I came from a tribe inland years ago and that is all I say about it.
The rowing boat? It is just south of my stall. Look that way and there it is, so you cannot miss it.
The dock is north-east a fair way. You pass the rowing boat first and then the burnt-out house, and there is Lilmoth Dock.
Ah, look at you, not a scratch on you this time, you see? Come and sit by the stall and tell me everything, friend. I have been saving the news for you.
Well, you are new here, are you not? Tired walk, that. I can see it. Buy something or tell me where you have been.

Black Marsh, you ask, as if it were one thing, you see? What I know is that an owing can be sold on, so if a holder is owed months by a debtor, he can sell those months to a man who needs hands. The worker goes with them.
There is a drinker called Deep-In-His-Cups. He sits out on the shore track, a short way north-east of my stall, and he talks to anyone who stays a while. I think he knows more than he lets on.

I am Okeeh-Jas. This is my stall, south side, where the rowboat comes in. I married into this village and I still talk like the city, they tell me. I trade with anyone who lands. I like the gossip as much as the coin.
I sell food and small goods from this stall, and the fish is fresh, whatever you may have heard. Look all you like. I will laugh at my own prices with you.
Wet, customer? A short way east of our bedrolls there is a door that leads indoors. A fighter should get out of the rain.
Walking Dead, customer. They walk outside Lilmoth's walls, and there are some a short way north-north-west of our bedrolls. Keep your fists up.
Lilmoth Dock, customer? Follow the boards east, just until the burnt-out house is on your right. Then go north-east a short way, and you will see the dock.
Ha! Look who it is, my friend. Sit by the fire. I am glad of a face that I trust.
Well, customer. Got coin, or just questions?
I am Haxal-Tei. I fight with my fists and I fight for whoever pays the band. I talk the terms, so if you want a job done, you talk to me.
The band is camped here. Heem-Tsal, the fire mage, is just west-south-west of these bedrolls, and Keeps-Both-Edges is just west of him. I trust Keeps-Both-Edges with my purse.

You mean the Dwemer ruin, ojel. Walk north-east a short way until the big ship is on your left, then follow the shore south-east just until you reach the burnt-out house, also on your left. From there climb east over open ground a fair way until you reach Soulrest on your left, then climb east a short way more, and the ruin is there.
Ah, I am glad of you. Sit by me and ask whatever you like. I will answer it properly.
Yes, ojel? If you want something, say it plainly. I was reading.

An alchemist would find all three plants useful, ojel. Jazbay, lavender and juniper share a patch just north-west of here. I would sooner see them gathered by someone who knows the difference between them. Precisely.
You ask about Black Marsh. Ask Flaa Heet how Lilmoth is governed. I would have written it down myself, but the tree-minders of Lilmoth refused to let me sit by the city's Hist and take notes.
I am Heem-Tsal. I cast fire for this band and read whatever I can get my claws on. I travel with them for the passage south. I have not yet found a reason to leave.
If you want a book, ojel, try Hereguard Plantation, a fair way west of here. The bookseller Looks-At-Books keeps her shelf there. I have heard of that shelf, and I intend to see it.
The gravestones lie north of Lilmoth's walls, a short way north-west of here, and the dead have risen among them. A crocodile lies in the water a short way west. Keep clear of both.
You. Good. Stand by me a moment. The track is quiet. I would like it to stay so.
You there. What do you want? Keep your hands where I can see them.
Dead trees stand along the shore track just north-east of here. The band camps among them.
I carry a blade in each hand. I keep the band's watch. I was a guard once. I will not tell you for whom.
Two Argonians loiter by the leeks to the north. Sheeh-Vos stands just north-north-east of here, Waits-For-Lanterns just north-east. I do not trust either one.
Flaa Heet, is it? Walk south-west a short way, fellow, until you come to the rowing boat. Then follow the shore south-west another short way, and the village is there.
The dock? It is just north-north-east of here, fellow, in plain sight along the shore. I have watched it long enough to know.
Ahh, my friend, my friend. Sit down and tell me you brought something to wet the throat. I will tell you about the boat again, if you will have it.
Hm? Oh. What do you want, fellow? I am only sitting.
Black Marsh is wide. I have seen only the water of it. There is a big ship tied up at the dock now, with steps going down beside it to the water. I watched them load her, I did, every crate.
There are three dead Dunmer lying at the east end of Lilmoth Dock, a short way north-north-east of here, and they have not been buried. I do not go near, fellow, but I notice who does.
Deep-In-His-Cups, they call me. I earned it. I was a boatman once, and I lost my boat. Sit a while and I will tell you how, fellow.
Come close, friend. Keep your voice low, eh? I know you. The dock is quiet.
Hsst. Do not stand over me, cousin. I am only picking leeks.
Leeks grow all around me here, and more just west-south-west. Pick them slowly and look bored while you do it.
Past the bodies at the dock's east end there is a chest, a short way east-north-east of here. Look in it before anyone else does.
Dunmer lie just north-east of here, and they have not been searched. Whoever gets to their pockets first keeps what is in them, so go quietly.
I am Sheeh-Vos. I gather what the dock loses. I do not ask who owned it. Do not look at my hands for too long.
Deep-In-His-Cups sits just south-south-east of here. He sees everything at the dock and remembers half of it. He is a better source than I am.
The Walking Dead wander outside the city walls, honoured guest, a short way north-west of here. I would not hurry past them. A patient man keeps to the shadows and lets them go by.
Ah. You came back, my friend. Stand here beside me, where the shadows are good, and tell me what you have seen.
Honoured guest. You speak to me in plain sight, which I would not have chosen. Say what you want, slowly.
A hungry man can eat on this shore, honoured guest. Gourds grow along it, a short way west-south-west of here. Take what you need.
Below the walls there is a door, a short way west-north-west of here. It leads indoors and is well out of the way. I will say no more than that.
There is a thing I know. I do not give it to a stranger, honoured guest. Come back when I have had cause to trust you. Perhaps I will speak then.

Look to the graves north of the walls, a short way north-west of here. There is a trapdoor in the ground that leads down under the city. The chest beside it has already been emptied, so do not expect a reward.

I am Waits-For-Lanterns. I plan small jobs and I wait for dark to do them. It is a slow season, honoured guest, nothing more. I stand nearest the dock, where I can count the lanterns and the guards between them.
The big ship, traveller? South a short way, along the boards. It lies at the dock. I would sooner be posted at that dock than here.
Temple Pass is north, traveller. Take the path north a short way, until you reach the dead tree on your right. Then cross the open ground north for a fair way. Temple Pass is there.
Oh, good, it is you! Stand with me a while. Ukka-Meesh has told me another story, and I want to tell it to you.
Be well, traveller. Do you have a question?
Tidings, traveller. I am on watch here, so speak quickly.
This is the middle of Thorn, traveller. The signpost is right beside me, to the south-west.
Who founded Thorn? Ask Ma-Veesk, traveller. Ukka-Meesh has told me some of it, but Ma-Veesk can tell it to you properly.
I am Xeech-Nu, traveller. I am new to the watch, and I listen to the stories of Ukka-Meesh, a guard here. I would like a post on the docks.
Ukka-Meesh, the guard at the centre, stands just east of here, traveller. I think he knows everything, and he tells me his stories when the watch is quiet.
I am a guard at the town's centre, traveller. New guards are posted to the centre until someone trusts them. I would rather be on the south dock.
Ah, it is you. Sit a while, my friend. I am only half awake, but I am glad of the company.
Mm. Yes, traveller? Speak slowly. I have been on watch a long time.
I keep watch over the east houses with Jeelus-Vax, traveller. The house lies just north-north-west of here.
Ask Tolyn Vedram about the painting of the Slave-Coffles, traveller. I have seen it too, and I do not like to speak of it.
I am Sleeps-Standing, traveller. I earned the name on a long watch. I guard the east houses.
Severan Otho, the hired Imperial soldier, stands just south-south-east of here, traveller.
I guard the east houses. The watch changes twice a day, traveller. The night is long.
Thorn, outlander? Follow the path south-west a short way, until the dead tree stands on your right. Then go south, and Thorn is just there.
I need not ask whose side you are on. Sit. I will see to the Owings after we talk.
Outlander. Whose side are you on?
There is a house just east of here. Look, but do not trouble the people in it. I am a soldier of the rising, outlander.
Heita-Meen? Fendyl Omoren is the one to ask, outlander. I know that story by heart, and I will tell it once I know whose side you are on.
Ask Jeelus-Vax about the title, outlander, though I think of Jeelus-Vax as a collar with a spear. The rising means to settle that title on those who work it.
I am Owes-Nothing. I took that name the day I walked off an Owing, and I fight for those who stood in Thorn when the Dres left.
Tallies-Twice is a Tax Heel, one of the field-owners' collectors of Owings and tolls. That thief is just north of here.
I am a soldier of the rising. We want every Owing in Thorn ended, and the title settled on those who work it.
Sit on the bench, tall one. It is just south-east of here. Your feet must be tired.

Longmont? Walk south-east to the bamboo hut, just there on your right. Then follow the shore south-east a short way until the giant tree stands on your right. Walk east from the tree a short way, and Longmont is there.
You came back, my friend! Did you come through the water or dry? Tell me everything. I counted you in.
You, tall one. Who are you? Where did you come from? Did you walk through the water? I saw your feet.
Lily pads? They float on the water just west of here. More float just west-south-west.
This is Low-Reed Village. I know every face in it. The rowing boat lies on the water just west of here. It is mine to guard. Do not touch it, tall one.
I am Ree-Nakka. I am a hatchling of this village. I mind the rowing boat. Who comes and who goes? I count them all. Who are you counting?
Mends-The-Nets works just east-south-east of here. That is the cleverest person in the village. Ixa-Mee plays just east. Ixa-Mee is a tattler. Keep your secrets from that one.

Stranger. Go east round the cliffs a short way, until you reach the giant tree. Then go west over open ground a fair way, until the burnt-out house is on your left. Go west a fair way more, and you will find the Dwemer ruin.
It is you. I am glad, my friend. I will not whisper this time.
Stranger. Your hands are empty. That is good.
Stranger. I am not to talk long. Please say what you need.
Lily pads float just east-south-east of here, stranger. Take them yourself.
This is Low-Reed Village. There is a bamboo hut just north of here with a bed roll in it. I sleep there.
I am Ixa-Mee, stranger. I was hatched here in Low-Reed Village, as was everyone I know.
Mends-The-Nets sits just south-west of here. Mends-The-Nets is kind to me.
I fetch for Mends-The-Nets, stranger. The village workbench is just north of here.
Alten Merihall, traveller. Walk south-west a short way, until the giant tree is on your right. Then go west over open ground a fair way, and you will be there.
Longmont is a plain way, traveller. Walk south-east a short way, until the giant tree is on your right. Then walk east a short way, and you will be there.
There is room by the nets. Sit while I work, friend. A knot holds better when two people talk over it.
Speak, traveller. My hands will keep working while you do.
This is Low-Reed Village, traveller. Two giant trees stand just south-south-east and just east-south-east of here. I have never wanted to live anywhere else.
A root-herald speaks for a village to outsiders. News, trade and terms all go through that one, traveller.
Turns-The-Clutch is the egg-tender of this village. Turns-The-Clutch keeps the clutch.
I am Mends-The-Nets. I have mended this village's nets since I was small. Half the villagers learned their knots from me.
Ixa-Mee is just north-east of here. I am fond of that one. Ree-Nakka is just west-north-west. That one will lead this village or ruin it.
I mend nets, traveller. The benches stand just north-east and just west of here, and the workbench just north-north-east. Frayed straps are not beyond me either.

The Dwemer ruin. Follow the shore north a short way until the giant tree stands on your left. Then climb west over open ground a fair way until the burnt-out house stands on your left. Go west a fair way more, and the ruin is there. Walk softly, walker.
Alten Merihall. Go south-west a short way until the giant tree stands on your right. Then walk west over open ground a fair way. The hall is there.
Ah, my friend. Sit by the water with me. The water is calm today.
Walker. Keep your voice low. The fish listen.
Walker. Step quietly on the bank.
Lily pads lie thick on the water just south-south-east and just south-east of here. Take them gently, walker. Do not splash.
The giant trees stand west-south-west and north-north-west of me, a little way off. I think they hear more than we know.
When two of us quarrel here, they choose one that both of them trust to hear it. Most often that is the tree-minder. Pays-Late holds that place now. I trust Pays-Late above all.
I am Xeech-Utsei. I fish this still water with a pole. It takes patience, walker.
Hulee-Tah is south-south-west of here, not far off. He is loud. Keep him away from my water.
Alten Merihall? Take the shore south-west a short way, until the giant tree stands on your right. Then cross the open ground west a fair way. Alten Merihall is there, outsider.

Longmont is easy. Walk south-east a short way and you will reach the giant tree. Then follow the shore east a short way until the rowing boat lies on your right. From there walk east a short way more. Longmont is there.
Ha! You came back, my friend. Stand by my hut and tell me what you have seen.
Outsider! You walk up to a man at his work. Speak, but mind the bamboo.
My hut is just west of here, with a bed roll inside. I built it first. I built it best. Out on the water, just east-north-east, lies a rowing boat.
Ask Mends-The-Nets about the root-herald. I only know that I would trade for less than any herald, and I say so loudly.
I am Hulee-Tah. I build and patch the bamboo huts of this village, my own first. I went once to trade at the road-houses. I came home sure that we do things better here.
Jaa-Kur is just south-east of here and helps me when I build. Xeech-Utsei is just north-north-east. You will find Xeech-Utsei idle.
I build bamboo huts. I want enough bamboo to raise a second one before the rains, outsider. A giant tree stands just north-west of here, as a mark for steering.
Big one, there is a bench just east-north-east of here. Bamboo is heavy and I sit on it when my arms are tired.

Longmont? Go south-east a short way, and you will see a giant tree, and keep it on your right. Then follow the shore east a fair way until you reach the dead tree, also on your right. Then walk east just a little, and Longmont is there.
Big one, big one, I am so glad! I kept the shallows warm for you. Did you bring something shiny this time?
Hello, big one. What did you bring with you?
There are lily pads just west-south-west of here and just east. They float in the shallows where I play.
This is the village and I carry bamboo here when there is bamboo to carry. There is a rowing boat out on the water, just north-north-east of here. Ree-Nakka is bossy and will not let me near it.
I am Jaa-Kur and I am the youngest hatchling here. I follow the hut-builder and carry whatever I am given. One day I will carry the long poles.
Hulee-Tah is by his hut, just north-west of here. He is the best of all of us and I want to be just like him.
The Way to Ruins? North-east, a short way. You will see it.
You came back. Good. Sit on the bench with me, because my feet have had enough for today.
You there. If you want something hauled, say so. I have lines to pull.
There is a bench just east-north-east of here. An iron door just north-east leads indoors. The houses are a short way off, south-south-east and east-south-east.
The Panther River forks near Helstrom. I grew up on it, so I know it well.
You there. Haj-Wan wants an outsider to go after her kin Sei-Wan, who walked out into the basin alone. She waits at Helstrom's gate. I haul lines and nothing else, so I keep out of it.
I am Hauls-Wet-Rope. The dock bosses gave me that name and I kept it. I came down the Panther River for the work.
Namorine is just south of here. You will find him on the easy loads. Do not ask me to walk you there.
I haul the lines and the loads for whoever pays, here at the north end. A Dwemer ruin rises just south of here, so you cannot miss the place. Look at my hands if you doubt the work.
The Way to Ruins? North-east of here, passenger, a short way off, and you cannot miss it. If it is Gih-Xaleel you want, the levy warden, take the path south. He is a short way along it.
Well, look who has come back! Sit with me a while, my friend. I have been waiting by these ruins. You are better company than the water.
Passenger? Are you looking for a boat? I wait here for anyone who wants carrying along the water. Tell me where you are bound and I will tell you what it costs.

This is Helstrom, and I think it is the finest city there is. The Dwemer ruins rise just south of here, one beside the other. There are iron doors too, just south-west and just south-east, if you want to go indoors.
Many people call Helstrom the immortal capital of the Argonians. I say they are right. I have seen other places on my fares, and no other place compares.
Rumours? Helstrom and Stormhold have been rivals for a long time. I carried fares as far as the Stormhold side once. The people there haggled me down every time, so I do not go back.
I am Namorine, the boatman. I wait here by the ruins for a fare. My mother gave me this name and I have kept it, though the people of Helstrom cannot place it. Ask me about the water if you like.
Hauls-Wet-Rope works just north of here. She works too hard. Bejeen-Ul stands a short way south. I like his company.
If you need to sit, visitor, a bench stands just south-south-east of here. Sit on it and keep your weight off the old walls.

Climb south a short way, visitor, until you reach the waterfall on your left. Then walk south-west a fair way until you reach the bridge on your left. Follow the shore south-west a short way until you reach the old stone columns on your left, then follow the shore south a short way more. Helstrom is there.
Welcome, my friend. Sit with me by the stone for a while. I am glad of your company.
Visitor. Mind the wall. It is old, so do not lean on it.
A Dwemer ruin stands right beside us, just east-south-east. Another stands just north-north-east. Houses stand just west and just west-south-west, with an iron door just west.
Ask Namorine what they call Helstrom. I like her talk. I think the city is older than anyone's story of it.
Haj-Wan waits at Helstrom's gate, visitor. Her kin Sei-Wan went into the basin by himself. She asks for an outsider to follow him. I patch walls and cannot leave them, but I hope an outsider goes.
I am Bejeen-Ul. I patch the old stonework in these streets for the assembly's levy. The assembly pays me late. I like stone that does not crumble when I touch it.
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden, keeps the gate a short way south of here. He is fair, visitor.
The alleys of Helstrom are counted both wonderful and dangerous, outlander. Keep your weapon sheathed in them and your eyes open.

Helstrom? Climb south-west, just until you reach the waterfall on your left. Then walk south-west a fair way, until you reach the bridge on your left. Follow the shore south-west a short way, until you reach the old stone columns on your left. Then follow the shore south a short way. Helstrom is there.
Way to Ruins? Follow the path north a short way, until you reach the old stone columns on your right. Then walk north-east a fair way. It is there.
Your face is known here and I have no complaint of you. The gate is quiet. Go through.
Outlander. State your business at this gate.
This is the gate of Helstrom, outlander. Dwemer ruins stand just south of me and just north-north-west. A stone tower stands just east-south-east.
A waterfall falls just south-west of here. Two bridges cross the water beside it, one just south-south-west and one just south-west. Do not wander far from the path.
Helstrom has never been taken by an army. After the Battle of Argonia the Empire never tried. The Imperial historians call our guard brutes. I do not care what they write.
I am Gih-Xaleel, a warden of Helstrom's levy. I keep this gate and I decide who goes in. Helstrom has never been taken, and I mean to see it stays so.
I sell nothing. I keep the gate. An iron door just north-north-west of here leads into a hall where a soldier of the levy stands guard.
Sells-Dear the boat captain is a short way west of here. Weesa-Nur is a short way west-south-west. Sells-Dear is sharp but honest.
The dock? Follow the shore south-east a short way. You cannot miss it. Mind where you put your feet on the way.
You again, my friend. Come in, but wipe your boots first. I will not have mud tracked through my house, not even by you.
Well. Look at the state of those boots. What do you want on my doorstep?
That is my door, just west of you. The house itself is just west-north-west. Keep off the step. There is a stone tower just south-west of here, and a Dwemer ruin just east.
Rumours? Ask Namorine about Helstrom and Stormhold. I hear plenty from my doorstep, but I do not give it away. The dock folk are thieves who sell it dear.
I keep this house. I have lived in Helstrom all my life. I sell what I can spare to the boats at the dock. Now, who are you?
Sells-Dear, the boat captain, stands just north-north-west of here. She ties up too close to my house.
I sell what I can spare to the boats at the dock. A bridge crosses a short way east of here, and the dock is a short way south-east. Count your change there, because the dock folk are all thieves.

Ruins, buyer? Climb east to the stone tower, it stands just there. Then follow the path north-east a short way, until the old stone columns are on your right. Walk north-east a fair way after that, and you are at Way to Ruins. I charge nothing for that walk. Hah.

The Dwarven Ruins will cost you good boots. Walk south a fair way, until the stone tower is on your right. Then follow the shore south a short way, until Helstrom is on your right. Then take the boards south a short way more, until the big ship is on your left. From there, ask again. The ruins lie further south-east. Hah.
Ah, I know that purse. For you the first price is the last price, friend. I will not even laugh while I say it.
Buyer! You look like you carry coin. Tell me what you need. I will tell you what it costs. Hah.
See the door close by, just west-north-west? That is a house, just north-west of here. A second door is just east. Hah.
A Dwemer ruin rises just north-north-east of here. Keep clear of it, buyer, unless you can pay for the trouble. Hah.
I am Sells-Dear. I run a boat out of Helstrom and I trade by it. I took a city name, because city buyers pay a city price to a city name. Hah.
Weesa-Nur lives just south-south-east of here. Be careful, buyer. She is a busybody who will count your coin before you do. Hah.
I trade by boat. Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza work the landing, a fair way south of here. They tell every customer I cheat them. I say they should buy a boat of their own. Hah.
Out in the deep interior food, tools and safe passage are worth more than coin. Remember that, buyer, when you are hungry and a boat is the only road. Hah.
Thorn, civilian? It lies north of here, a short walk. Don't dawdle.
Stand easy. The ship's quiet and the men are paid.
State your business, civilian. I've men to pay and a ship to mind.
Well, civilian? Say it plainly, I haven't the time for talk.
These are the south docks. The big ship is just east of here, and I'd keep clear of it.
Thorn's name? Ask Bites-The-Coin, civilian. I keep my men paid and in order, and I've no more to say about the town.
That's not for a stranger. I'll say it once, civilian. There's cargo behind the ship's door, just east of here, that's on no tally. Repeat it and you'll answer to me.
Aulus Varrenius, sergeant. I lead a company that came on the big ship and hires out to the field-owners hereabouts. We serve no Empire; there's been none here for two centuries.
Decimus Pell, archer of my company, is just south-south-east of here. Ask him what you like, civilian. Keep it short.
It's you. Good. Stand where I can see the wind on you and tell me what you need.
Stranger. State your business, and keep your hands where I can see them.
The dock is just north-east of here, stranger. You won't miss it.
The Owing? Its defenders say it is theirs by right. It came out of their own arbitration. It ends. A prison does not. I'd call that fair.
Decimus Pell. I came with Aulus Varrenius's company, and I guard the ship with a bow. I keep to myself, stranger.
Quintus Albero. Young soldier of our company. Just east-north-east of here. You'll hear him before you reach him.
I'm an archer. The company guards whoever pays it, and the field-owners pay now. That's the whole of it, stranger.
Oh, I was hoping you'd come by! It's good to talk to someone who isn't in the company. I'll tell you, I've been thinking of home all morning.
Good day, sir or madam. Is there something I can do for you? I'm only one of the soldiers, mind, so I may not know much.
Oh! Hello. Sorry, I didn't see you there. What can I do for you?
This place? Truth be told, I'm still working out what to make of it; it's nothing like home. The door is just east of here, if that's what you're after.
The Empire's been gone from Black Marsh for two hundred years, sir. Imperial people stayed on, but the flag didn't, and I'd gone and thought I was joining the Legion.
Black Marsh? Two hundred years the Empire's been gone from it, they tell me. Plenty of our own people stayed on, but you won't find our flag, and I do keep looking for it.
Me? Quintus Albero, sir, the youngest in the company. I miss home something terrible. I can't stop talking about it, as you'll have noticed.
If it's someone from the company you want, sir, our corporal, Marius Lentulo, is just north-north-east of here.

I'm with the hired company, sir. We sign on for a season and are paid at the end of it; not what I pictured when I put my name down, I'll admit. Decimus Pell, one of the company, still calls me 'boy', and he's cold with it.
Thorn? Follow the boards north-west a short way and you're there. Hard to miss, traveller.
Well, you know the dock by now. Mind the boards, the tide has them wet. I've a minute, if you want it.
Traveller. What can I do for you? Quickly, if you can; I've stores to see to.
Well, traveller. State your business, or let me get on. I cannot stop the tide for either of us.
The dock? Just north-north-west of where I'm standing, traveller. Watch the tide on the planks.
The Empire? Quintus Albero is the one to ask, traveller. I know it's gone and I don't miss it. I've stores to see to.
Marius Lentulo, corporal in Aulus Varrenius's company, and its quartermaster. My grandfather was a Legion man. I'm a hired man, traveller. I carry no flag.
Aulus Varrenius, sergeant of our hired company, is just south-west of here. I trust him, which is more than I say of most.
I'm the company's quartermaster. We keep our stores on the ship and sell what we can't eat, traveller. All I ask is that supplies come in on time.
The big ship? Follow the boards just south, and when you have it on your right, turn south-east along the boards. It's right there, traveller.
You'll want the big ship. Keep to the boards south just until it's on your right; after that it's the boards south-east, and you're at it.
Stop a while and tell me how you've been; I've no one else to talk to about nothing in particular.
Come and stand with me a moment; there's no hurry. I'm glad of the talk.
Good day, traveller. That's an accent I can't quite place. What can I do for you?
Traveller. Keep to the boards and you'll come to no harm. Something I can help with?
Not much to it from where I stand, traveller. You can see the dock from here, just south-south-east, if that's what you're after.
Ask Quintus Albero about the Empire, traveller; I can't tell you much of it. I was born here. Black Marsh is the only home I know.
Gaius Fennic, traveller. I was born in Black Marsh of Imperial parents, and I speak a little Jel besides. I've never seen the Empire, so I count myself as from here.
That's Holds-The-Tally, the guard at the south dock, standing just south of here. I like him; he's a good sort, and he'll tell you straight.
I'm one of the company's men, posted between the docks and the centre. We stand where the field-owners say, and that's about the size of it.
Cage Door? Easy, stranger. Head north just until you reach the dead tree on your right, then take the path north-west, and Cage Door is right there. Can't miss it.
Ha, there you are, my friend! Stand clear of the target line and stay a while. I'm feeling lucky today, and I have thrown well.
Stranger. Mind where you stand, I'm shooting. What d'you want?
Thorn? A fine place to get rich, stranger, if you've got nerve. The hut is just west-north-west of here, if it's a bed you're after.
Ask Bites-The-Coin what Thorn is called, stranger. I like her, and I'd bet she tells it better than I would.
Lucan Sevro, archer, hired by the Imperial company. I guard the centre with my bow, and I'm the best shot in Thorn. Ask anyone. Or better, bet on it.
Sheel-Taza is a guard, just south-west of here. Sour as old milk, so don't expect a smile.
Stay a while, if you like; I've nothing to watch but the crowd, and your company's better.
Traveller. Is there something you need?
Good day, traveller. How can I help you?
If it's your bearings you want, traveller, the signpost is just south-south-east of here. The rest of the town I'm still learning myself.
Ask Holds-The-Tally about the villages around Thorn, traveller. I am still learning who really rules here, and Holds-The-Tally is clever.
I'm Tertius Vallo, a soldier of the hired Imperial company. I stand here and watch the town; that's most of the work.
Gaius Fennic, a soldier of our company, is just east-south-east of here. You'll find him there, traveller.
I'm a soldier of the hired company, traveller. Our posts run from the docks up to the signposts at the centre, and mine is just south of them.
Well. You've kept your head down and your hands clean, which is more than most manage. Good to see you, my friend.
I'm on watch, civilian. State your business and keep your voice down.
Yes, civilian? Ask what you need to ask. I'm on duty.
The signposts are just south-south-west of here, civilian. Read them before you go wandering about.
Ask Decimus Pell why the Owing is defended, civilian. I hold that it is fair, and I keep order on that footing.
Rufio Casca, soldier of the company. I guard the west cages with the Argonian guards, and I say the Owing is fair to anyone who asks.
Wazei-Ru has the cage doors on the west side, just north-north-east of here. Soft on the prisoners, and I've told Wazei-Ru so.
The company keeps watch on the west cages for the field-owners, civilian. We keep the doors shut and the prisoners where they belong.
Temple Pass, traveller? Follow the path north a short way, until you reach the stone tower on your left. Then walk north over open ground a fair way, and you are there. Go steady.
Sit a moment if you like. My feet are glad of the excuse.
Traveller. I guard the houses on this side, so keep to the path and we'll have no trouble.
This is the east side, where I stand guard with Jeelus-Vax. The house is just east-north-east of here, if that's the one you want.
Ask Jeelus-Vax about the title, traveller. I think that question is the real fight in Thorn, whatever else you hear.
Severan Otho, soldier of the hired company. Jeelus-Vax and I watch the east houses. It's honest work, traveller, though I'll be glad to go home.
Nalvos Brenur? A Dunmer labourer, held under an Owing, so he works off a debt. He's just south of me, and he's a clever one.
Thorn? Follow the path just south-west until you reach the dead tree on your right. Then go just south, and you are in Thorn, party.
For you I have a moment. Speak, and I will hear it.
You are a stranger to me, party. State your business.
Well, party? I have accounts to close. Be brief.
This is Thorn, party. The hut is just north-north-east of here.
Ask Nalvos Brenur about the ledger, party. I keep it and I collect on it. I am not paid to explain it, party.
I am Quill-Teeth, party, one of the Tax Heel. That is what the people of Thorn call the collectors the field-owners send. I am very good at my work.
Doveth Aralen is a Dunmer held under an Owing, and the eldest of the house's labourers. You will find Doveth just south-south-east of here. Doveth is slow, party, so ask and then wait.
I collect Owings for the field-owners, party. I also keep the ledger. A person called Owes-Nothing wants it burned, because Owes-Nothing is a debtor in hiding.
The stone tower, party? Climb north-west a short way. A short way, no more. The tower is there.
It is good to see your face again, party. I do not say that to many.
Party. Say what you want, and say it plainly. I see you are armed, so keep your hand away from the blade while you talk.
This is the north side, party, near the houses. A house stands just south-east of here.
Ask Mils Ganthis about the charges on an Owing, party. I check every sum I write twice.
Decimus Pell is the one to ask about the Owing, party. I say it is fair because it ends.
I am Tallies-Twice. I collect on the north side for the field-owners, and I face the rising across the north houses. I want it gone from this side.
Breaks-The-Ledger is a soldier of the rising against the Owings. He is just west of here, party. Keep your weapon near when you go; I say he will strike.
I am a Tax Heel, party. Tolls and Owings on the north side are mine to collect. I check every sum twice. Twice, always.
Stand with us, then. A sharp blade is always welcome here.
Outlander. Say what you want, or leave me.
Why do you interrupt me, outlander? I have work to do.
There is nothing here but open ground, outlander. The house is just south of here.
Ask Fendyl Omoren about Heita-Meen, outlander. I know the story, and I mean to finish it.
Ask Nalvos Brenur about the families of Thorn, outlander. Mine is a mixed one, and I will say no more of it.
I am Breaks-The-Ledger. I fight for the rising, outlander. That is all you need to know.
Owes-Nothing is a soldier of the rising, like me. You will find him just south-east of here. He is slower than I would like.
I fight in the rising. We mean to break the Tax Heel's ledgers before anything else. The Tax Heel collect Owings and tolls for the field-owners.
Ask Gih-Xaleel about the alleys, and wipe your feet before you come in. I keep this floor clean.
You again. Come in out of the wet, friend. Mind the floor, though.
You. State your business, or move on.
This is the hall. The iron door opens on the street by the gate, just north-north-west of the warden's post. Stay inside if you have sense.
Helstrom has a name for being dangerous. The city has never been taken. I have heard worse tales than that.
Ask Namorine about Stormhold. I say the Stormhold folk are soft. I say it to anyone who asks.
Levy soldier. I guard this hall. I would sooner be indoors than on the street.
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden. He keeps the gate, just outside that door. Go and see him.

take: Short and easy. I followed markers: report to Nesh-Deeka, take the ship, reach Helstrom, tell Ei-Tuja. The wasps never showed up, so that warning led nowhere.
